ws-che-buoi.title: Old-Alley Authentic Chè Bưởi & Pomelo Blossom Cooking
ws-che-buoi.titleVi: Nấu Chè Bưởi Cổ Truyền Hương Hoa Bưởi Tại Con Hẻm Bàn Cờ
ws-che-buoi.address: Hẻm 242/18 Nguyễn Thiện Thuật, Phường 3, Quận 3, TP. Hồ Chí Minh
ws-che-buoi.history: Southern Chè Bưởi originated as a seasonal dessert in the Mekong Delta and Saigon. Bà Ba learned the recipe from her grandmother in the late 1960s, preserving handcrafting techniques for over 45 years.
techniques: Brining and massaging white pomelo pith (cùi bưởi) with coarse sea salt to extract bitterness completely.
Soaking in warm alum water, washing repeatedly, and rolling thoroughly in pure tapioca flour.
Rapid boiling to create crispy translucent gems (những viên cùi bưởi trong veo, giòn sần sật).
Gently folding steamed golden split mung beans into fragrant pomelo flower nectar and warm coconut cream.
ingredients: Fresh Năm Roi Pomelo Pith (Cùi bưởi Năm Roi)
Steamed Split Mung Beans (Đậu xanh xát vỏ)
Organic Tapioca Starch (Bột năng nguyên chất)
Natural Distilled Pomelo Blossom Extract (Nước hoa bưởi chưng cất truyền thống)
Fresh Coconut Milk (Nước cốt dừa tươi)
Crushed Toasted Peanuts (Đậu phộng rang vàng giòn)
allergens: Peanuts (toasted peanut garnish — host can completely omit upon advance request)
etiquetteTips: Please remove your shoes before stepping into the family living quarters.
Greet the elder host with two hands slightly clasped as a sign of respect ('Dạ con chào Bà').
Warm lotus or jasmine tea is served first before starting the kitchen hearth.

ws-bamboo-weaving.title: Living Heritage Bamboo Weaving & Coaster Crafting
ws-bamboo-weaving.titleVi: Nghệ Thuật Đan Lát Mây Tre Thủ Công & Chuyện Nghề Sông Nước
ws-bamboo-weaving.address: 88/4 Bình Quới, Cư xá Thanh Đa, Bình Thạnh, TP. Hồ Chí Minh
ws-bamboo-weaving.history: Bamboo is Vietnam's spiritual tree — resilient, pliable, and communal. Chú Tư preserves rural craft traditions brought to Saigon by migrant riverway artisans in the mid-20th century.
techniques: Shaving and splitting soaked green bamboo stalks into paper-thin, flexible ribbons (chuốt nan tre).
Traditional cross-hatch herringbone weaving pattern (đan nong mốt, nong hai).
Hand-binding the circular outer rim using organic hemp cords and sealing with natural tree beeswax.
ingredients: Smoked pliable bamboo strips (Nan tre ngâm dẻo)
Organic hemp cords (Dây gai tự nhiên)
Natural beeswax sealant (Sáp ong rừng bóng mờ)
etiquetteTips: Watch the artisan's hand positions closely before applying force with shaping knives.
Never step across raw bamboo strips laid on the craft mat.
Handle tools with two hands when passing them to the elder craftsman.

ws-nambo-pottery.title: Nam Bộ Handcrafted Terracotta & Alleyway Kiln Pottery
ws-nambo-pottery.titleVi: Vuốt Gốm Đất Đỏ Nam Bộ & Nặn Đồ Gia Dụng Truyền Thống
ws-nambo-pottery.hostName: Nghệ Nhân Năm Gốm (Lê Văn Năm)
ws-nambo-pottery.address: 12 Lò Gốm, Phường 8, Quận 5, TP. Hồ Chí Minh
ws-nambo-pottery.history: Saigon's historic Lò Gốm quarter was the beating heart of Southern ceramic trade along the Tàu Hủ canal from the 18th to late 20th century.
techniques: Wedging and kneading natural red alluvial clay from the Đồng Nai riverbed.
Centering and pulling vessels on a low Southern kickwheel (bàn xoay chân gỗ).
Decorating with traditional comb incisions and hand-applying ash-rice husk glazes.
ingredients: Southern red clay (Đất sét đỏ phù sa)
Natural wood ash & rice husk glaze (Men tro trấu)
Carving stylus & wooden ribs
etiquetteTips: Aprons are provided; please roll up sleeves above elbows.
Work gently with clay dust — wash hands in designated sediment basins.

ws-silk-embroidery.title: Bảo Lộc Mulberry Silk Embroidery & Lotus Petal Art
ws-silk-embroidery.titleVi: Thêu Tay Chỉ Tơ Tằm Bảo Lộc & Họa Tiết Sen Cổ Điển
ws-silk-embroidery.hostName: Cô Lan Thêu (Võ Thị Hoàng Lan)
ws-silk-embroidery.address: 45/2 Đinh Tiên Hoàng, Phường Đa Kao, Quận 1, TP. Hồ Chí Minh
ws-silk-embroidery.history: Traditional hand-embroidery on pure Vietnamese mulberry silk reflects centuries of aristocratic and everyday textile heritage.
techniques: Stretching pure raw silk onto wooden tambour hoops.
Splitting fine silk threads into 4 or 8 micro-strands for gradient shading (chỉ tơ tơ tằm).
Executing delicate satin stitches (thêu đâm xô) to shade realistic lotus flower petals.
ingredients: 100% Bảo Lộc Mulberry Silk Canvas
Naturally dyed silk threads (Chỉ tơ nhuộm thảo mộc)
Bamboo tambour hoop & fine Japanese needles
etiquetteTips: Keep hands clean and dry before touching silk fabric.
Work in relaxed silence to appreciate needle rhythm.

ws-lotus-tea.title: Sacred Lotus Blossom Tea Scenting Ceremony
ws-lotus-tea.titleVi: Nghệ Thuật Ướp Trà Sen Bách Diệp Tây Hồ & Đạo Trà Việt
ws-lotus-tea.address: 18A/4 Ngô Thời Nhiệm, Phường Võ Thị Sáu, Quận 3, TP. Hồ Chí Minh
ws-lotus-tea.history: Vietnamese lotus tea is known as the king of teas, once reserved exclusively for royal courts.
techniques: Placing wild Shan Tuyết ancient tea leaves directly into blooming hundred-petal lotus blossoms at dawn.
Gentle drying over clay charcoal hearths to capture pure floral essential oils.
Brewing in miniature Yixing teapots with pure 85°C mountain spring water.
ingredients: Wild Shan Tuyết Old-Growth Tea (Trà Shan Tuyết cổ thụ)
Fresh West Lake 100-petal Lotus Blossoms (Hoa sen Bách Diệp)
Mountain spring water
etiquetteTips: Turn off mobile phone ringers to preserve serene tea meditation.
Receive the hot tea cup with both hands.

ws-banh-xeo.title: Crispy Southern Bánh Xèo Crepe & Wild Herb Foraging
ws-banh-xeo.titleVi: Đổ Bánh Xèo Miền Tây Giòn Rụm & Rau Rừng Vườn Nhà
ws-banh-xeo.address: 33/7 Trần Khắc Chân, Phường Tân Định, Quận 1, TP. Hồ Chí Minh
ws-banh-xeo.history: Bánh Xèo is the iconic sizzle of Southern Vietnam home kitchens, named after the loud sizzle ('xèo xèo') when batter hits lard in a smoking cast-iron wok.
techniques: Stone-milling wet rice batter blended with golden turmeric and fresh coconut milk.
High-heat wok swirling for paper-thin lace edges (viền bánh giòn tan).
Wrapping hot crepe slices in assorted wild leaves: lá cóc, lá xoài non, cải bẹ xanh, lá lốt.
ingredients: Fresh ground rice flour & turmeric root
Mekong river shrimp & thinly sliced pork belly
Bean sprouts & mung beans
Wild garden herbs (Rau rừng Tây Nam Bộ)
Garlic chili lime fish sauce
etiquetteTips: Bánh Xèo is best eaten with bare hands by wrapping with wild herbs.
Dip generously in fish sauce and enjoy in a single bite.
